title: Half the cases were vaccinated
hook: Nearly half the cases were vaccinated. Does that mean the vaccine failed?

knows: vaccines lower the risk of infection
the difference between a count and a rate
doesNotKnow: that the share of cases who are vaccinated depends on how many people are vaccinated

misconception: If about half of the cases were vaccinated people, the vaccine does not work.
objective: The learner can explain that when most people are vaccinated, vaccinated people can make up a large share of cases even when the vaccine cuts each person's risk by 90%, and that the right comparison is risk per person in each group.

claims.text: With 1,000 people, 90% vaccinated, everyone exposed, 50% unvaccinated risk and a vaccine that cuts risk by 90%: 50 unvaccinated cases and 45 vaccinated cases, so about 47% of cases (45 of 95) are vaccinated.
claims.source: 100 x 0.5 = 50; 900 x 0.05 = 45; 45 / 95 = 0.474 (checked with node). The stage uses expected counts, not random draws.

claims.text: At 100% vaccinated every case is vaccinated, yet there are 50 cases instead of 500 when nobody is vaccinated.

The share of cases who are vaccinated depends on vaccine coverage: with effectiveness VE and coverage PPV, the vaccinated share of cases PCV satisfies VE = 1 - [PCV/(1 - PCV)] x [(1 - PPV)/PPV]. To judge a vaccine, compare risk per person in each group.
claims.source: Orenstein et al. (1985), 'Field evaluation of vaccine efficacy', Bulletin of the World Health Organization 63(6): 1055-1068 (screening method). Check with the stage numbers: PCV = 45/95, PPV = 0.9 gives 1 - 0.9 x 0.111 = 0.90. Halloran, Longini & Struchiner (2010), Design and Analysis of Vaccine Studies, Springer.

claims.text: The numbers are made up; the model assumes everyone is equally exposed and the vaccine works the same for everyone.
claims.source: Modelling choice in Demo.tsx (RISK_VAX = 0.05, RISK_UNVAX = 0.5, expected counts).

recall.question: In a town where 95% of people are vaccinated, 60% of cases are vaccinated people. Does that show the vaccine fails?
options: No: compare the risk per person in each group
Yes, unless there were no cases at all
recall.why: With 95% vaccinated, the vaccinated group is 19 times bigger, so it can fill most of the case list even at much lower risk per person. These figures fit a vaccine that cuts risk by about 92%.
